;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2020 Malian protests]], [[2020 Malian coup d'état]]
**Gunfire and a [[mutiny]] take place at a [[military base]] in [[Kati]], [[Koulikoro Region|Koulikoro]], [[Mali]]. [[Malian Armed Forces|Soldiers]] arrest senior military officers as the [[government of Mali|government]] deploys troops to the area. [https://apnews.com/54737684e3e2a84f9b44656de7343e56 (AP)]
**The [[Office de Radiodiffusion-Télévision du Mali]] (ORTM) [[headquarters]] in the capital [[Bamako]] are evacuated amid reports of a [[Coup d'état|coup]] attempt. The French and Norwegian embassies urge their citizens to remain indoors after being notified of mutiny in the Armed Forces. [https://www.dw.com/en/possible-coup-underway-in-mali/a-54608009 (DW)]
**Two security forces later confirm to [[Reuters]] that [[President of Mali|President]] [[Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta]] and Prime Minister [[Boubou Cissé]] have been detained by the mutinying forces. The two men are believed to have been transported to [[Kati]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200818-ecowas-calls-on-mali-soldiers-to-end-the-mutiny (France 24)] [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/gunshots-heard-at-military-camp-near-mali-capital/1945667 (Anadolu Agency)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/gunfire-heard-mali-army-base-warnings-mutiny-200818111723901.html (Al Jazeera)]
**Bamako and the Presidential Palace is reportedly under the control of coup forces with tanks and other military vehicles on the streets. Anti-government protesters set fire to a [[Ministry of Justice (Mali)|Ministry of Justice]] building, while hundreds of opposition supporters gather on the streets to celebrate the coup. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-53825673 (BBC News)]
**The [[European Union]]'s [[High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy]] [[Josep Borrell]] condemns the attempted coup, rejecting any anticonstitutional change and calls for dialogue. He also announces that contacts are being made to decide the international community's response. [https://eeas.europa.eu/headquarters/headquarters-homepage/84191/mali-d%C3%A9claration-du-haut-repr%C3%A9sentantvice-president-josep-borrell-sur-la-tentative-de-coup-d_fr (European Union)]
*[[Islamic terrorism in Europe]]; [[Terrorism in Germany]]
**Three motorcyclists are rammed and left seriously wounded on a motorway in [[Berlin]], [[Germany]] during a [[vehicle-ramming attack]]. The perpetrator is arrested and identified as an [[Islamic extremism|Islamic extremist]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53832113 (BBC News)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[August 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
***14 rockets strike [[Kabul]], wounding ten people. The rockets mostly struck the diplomatic "Green Zone", which is home to several [[embassies]] and the [[NATO]] [[Resolute Support Mission|Resolute Support]] [[headquarters]]. Two suspects were arrested in connection with the attack, which the [[Taliban]] has denied responsibility for. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-afghanistan-attack/rocket-attack-in-kabul-wounds-at-least-10-triggers-embassy-lockdowns-idUKKCN25E0HV (Reuters)]
*[[Russian military intervention in the Syrian Civil War]]
**A [[Russia]]n [[Major_general#Russia|major general]] is [[Russian Armed Forces casualties in Syria|killed]] and two others are injured by a [[roadside bomb]] in [[Syria]] while en route to [[Hmeimim Air Base]] from [[Deir ez-Zor]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/russian-major-general-killed-in-explosion-in-syria/1945894 (Anadolu Agency)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 California wildfires]]
**[[Governor of California|California Governor]] [[Gavin Newsom]] declares a [[state of emergency]] to ensure the state receives vital resources as at least 27 [[List of California wildfires|wildfires]] are raging across the state, exacerbating a stifling heat wave. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/weather/california-declares-state-of-emergency-as-it-fights-fires-extreme-weather/ar-BB187s7o?ocid=msedgdhp (NBC News via msn.com)]
*[[2020 Masbate earthquake]]
**A 6.6-magnitude [[list of earthquakes in the Philippines|earthquake]] hits [[Cataingan]], [[Masbate]], [[Philippines]], with at least one person reported to have been killed. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/asia/philippines-earthquake-today-masbate-cataingan-death-toll-a9675236.html (''The Independent'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] is slated to make face masks mandatory for all shared spaces in offices and factories where there is more than one employee present. The measure is set to begin on September 1. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53817383 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] rules out easing further COVID-19-related public health restrictions amidst a rise in new cases. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200818-merkel-rules-out-easing-coronavirus-rules-as-german-cases-spike (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****[[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] "significantly" tightens restrictions after a rapid increase in the number of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases over the past two weeks. All businesses are told to let employees work from home, new limits are placed on outdoor gatherings, and the government warns people to avoid public transport. The new rules will be in place until at least September 13. [https://news.sky.com/story/coronavirus-ireland-significantly-tightens-restrictions-in-fight-to-control-covid-19-outbreaks-12051912 (Sky News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Prime Minister of Russia|Prime Minister]] [[Mikhail Mishustin]] announces that [[Ministry of Energy (Russia)|Energy Minister]] [[Alexander Novak]] has tested positive for COVID-19. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/russian-energy-minister-tests-positive-for-covid-19/1945324 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]] announces that his country has signed a deal with the British-Swedish pharmaceutical company [[AstraZeneca]] to manufacture a vaccine against COVID-19 that the company is developing with the [[Oxford Vaccine Group]]. The vaccine is currently in [[Phases of clinical research#Phase III|Phase III efficacy trials]] and AstraZeneca says it is targeting a formulation of results by the end of the year. Morrison states that the deal also allows citizens to receive immediate and free access to the vaccines, if successful. [https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/australasia/article/3097866/coronavirus-australia-will-manufacture-vaccine-and-give-it (AFP via ''SCMP'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Lebanon]]
***The acting [[Government of Lebanon|government]] reimposes a curfew for two weeks amid a spike in COVID-19 infections. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/coronavirus/2020/08/18/Coronavirus-Lebanon-reimposes-lockdown-amid-COVID-19-spike (Al Arabiya)]

;International relations
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the military]]
**[[South Korea–United States relations]], [[Korean conflict]]
***The [[United States Armed Forces]] resume joint [[military exercise]]s with the [[Republic of Korea Armed Forces]] after several COVID-19 cases were confirmed at [[United States Forces Korea]] bases since February. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2020/08/18/news/latest-stories/us-south-korea-begin-joint-military-drills-after-virus-delay/757179/ (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]
*[[Belarus–Lithuania relations]], [[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**[[Lithuania]]n MPs approve [[economic sanction]]s against [[Belarus]] over the contested presidential elections. Lithuanian Foreign Minister [[Linas Antanas Linkevičius|Linas Linkevičius]] says Lithuania is "sending a strong message to the world" and refuses to recognize [[Alexander Lukashenko]] as President. [https://apnews.com/4308f39f7fd8e40ad4f7d551fa53f9cb (AP)]

;Law and crime
*[[Assassination of Rafic Hariri]]
**The [[Special Tribunal for Lebanon]] finds Salim Ayyash, a senior member of [[Lebanon|Lebanese]] militant group [[Hezbollah]], guilty of [[assassinating]] former [[Prime Minister of Lebanon|Prime Minister]] [[Rafic Hariri]] in [[Beirut]] in 2005, following a five-year trial. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/18/hezbollah-member-found-guilty-over-killing-rafik-hariri-lebanon (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2010 G20 Toronto summit protests]]
**The [[Toronto Police Service]] agrees to pay compensation of [[Canadian dollar|C$]]16.5 million ([[United States dollar|US$]]12.5M) to about 1,100 protesters who were wrongfully arrested in [[Toronto|the city]] during the [[2010 G20 Toronto summit|2010 G20 summit]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/18/g20-protesters-toronto-police-canada (''The Guardian'')]
*[[MV Wakashio oil spill|MV ''Wakashio'' oil spill]]
**[[Mauritius Police Force|Police]] in [[Mauritius]] arrest the Captain of the ship which spilled huge amounts of [[petrol]] off the coast of the country, causing a major environmental disaster. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mauritius-environment/mauritius-arrests-captain-of-stricken-japanese-oil-tanker-idUSKCN25E1UV?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Papua New Guinea]] [[Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary|police]] officers shoot and kill 11 prisoners after a mass [[jailbreak]] on Friday. At least 34 prisoners remain at large. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/423817/eleven-prisoners-killed-during-mass-jailbreak-in-png (RNZ)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 United States Postal Service crisis]]
**[[U.S. Postmaster General]] [[Louis DeJoy]], in response to politicians' criticism that proposed changes to U.S. mail services could slow the handling of mail-in ballots, suspends all mail service changes until after the November election. He also said there will be no changes to retail hours at post offices, mail collection boxes will remain where they are, and no mail processing facilities will be closed. A number of states, including [[Washington (state)|Washington]] and [[New York (state)|New York]], said they are planning legal moves to block the Postal Service changes. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-election-post-office/trumps-postmaster-general-pauses-service-cuts-after-mail-in-ballots-outcry-idUSKCN25E1Q2 (Reuters)]
*[[Politics of Equatorial Guinea]]
**[[President of Equatorial Guinea|President]] [[Teodoro Obiang]] appoints [[Francisco Pascual Obama Asue|Obama Asue]] as [[Prime Minister of Equatorial Guinea|Prime Minister]] again, four days after he resigned generating criticism from the opposition. [https://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/20200818/482902011935/obama-asue-designado-de-nuevo-como-primer-ministro-de-guinea-ecuatorial.html (''La Vanguardia'')]
